newsitem.title: USA: Sensus gets orphan status for hormone disease drug.
newsitem.headline: Sensus gets orphan status for hormone disease drug.

text.p: Sensus Corp said Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has designated Trovert, a growth hormone antagonist, an Orphan Drug for the treatment of acromegaly, a degenerative condition which may result in premature death.

According to Sensus, about 40,000 people around the world suffer from this disease, which is marked by the development of coarse facial features, enlarged joints and thickened bones, swelling of soft tissue and the enlargement of the tongue, heart and other internal organs.
Orphan drug designations are given to drugs and biologics which treat medical conditions affecting 200,000 people or less, and for which adequate cures or treatments do not exist.
Sensus said it recently entered Phase II clinical trials for Trovert for the treatment of acromegaly and expects to begin Phase II studies in diabetes shortly.
Sensus was formed in 1994 to develop and market novel drugs based on the antagonism of human growth hormone. The company is headquartered in Austin, Texas.
